title: Student notes: carbon in restored tidal marshes
bodyMd:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes.

- Tidal marshes store carbon in waterlogged soil, where decay is slow.
- In 2023 ecologist Hana Vrbova surveyed 32 restored tidal marshes along one coastline.
- Marshes restored fewer than 10 years earlier stored an average of 1.2 kilograms of carbon per square metre.
- Marshes restored more than 30 years earlier stored an average of 4.6 kilograms of carbon per square metre.
- Vrbova concluded that carbon storage in a restored marsh builds up slowly over decades.
accessibilityText: A list of five student research notes. One: tidal marshes store carbon in waterlogged soil where decay is slow. Two: in 2023 ecologist Hana Vrbova surveyed 32 restored tidal marshes along one coastline. Three: marshes restored fewer than 10 years earlier stored on average 1.2 kilograms of carbon per square metre. Four: marshes restored more than 30 years earlier stored on average 4.6 kilograms of carbon per square metre. Five: Vrbova concluded that carbon storage in a restored marsh builds up slowly over decades.

provenance.notes: Original notes written for this item bank. The ecologist, the survey and all figures are invented.
